gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ wear badges at all times inside the plant.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' = a rule that has to be followed.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a mistake — I ordered the vegetarian option.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses the speaker's certainty about a present situation: must be.

gaps.sentence: You ___ be starving — you haven't eaten since breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses a logical deduction about the present.

gaps.sentence: The ground is wet, so it ___ have rained overnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Must have' plus the participle draws a certain conclusion about the past: must have rained.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.sentence: You really ___ to apologise before this gets worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses advice similar to 'should': ought to apologise.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: There was plenty of food left, so the guests ___ have been hungry.
gaps.explanation: The evidence (leftover food) rules out hunger: can't have been.
